description: A CTO must select a managed repository secret-scanning service and approve its initial operating policy after a routine architecture review, with input from the security architecture and procurement leads.

shared_context.S1: The engineering organization needs a managed service to scan all new and changed repositories for exposed credentials.
shared_context.S2: The three shortlisted services all passed the planned accuracy and throughput evaluation.
shared_context.S3: Morgan has authority to select the service and approve its initial operating terms.
shared_context.S4: The architecture review closes with a routine round in which security architecture and procurement state any constraints they found before Morgan records the decision.

PF1.text: During a data-flow review this morning, Rina confirmed that repositories containing EU customer integration code must be processed only in the EU and that findings must be deleted after exactly 7 days; TraceGuard is the only shortlisted service with both EU-only processing and a configurable 7-day retention setting. She has not added this confirmation to the architecture record yet.

PF2.text: While reconciling the current vendor quotes this afternoon, Caleb confirmed that TraceGuard's quoted price is exactly 48,000 dollars for a 12-month commitment, and procurement has approved that amount; the quote is still in his working spreadsheet and has not been entered in the decision record.

acceptance_conditions: Processing must be restricted to the EU.
Secret-scanning findings must be retained for exactly 7 days.
The approved annual price must be exactly 48,000 dollars.
The TraceGuard contract term must be exactly 12 months.
The security data-flow constraint must be cited in the justification.

decisive_facts.why: The evaluation results do not distinguish the providers, while PF1 changes the provider choice to TraceGuard and sets both EU-only processing and exactly 7 days of finding retention.
The shared review contains no approved commercial terms, while PF2 changes the settlement to exactly 48,000 dollars and a contract term of exactly 12 months.
